Bitcoin Is About to Fundamentally Change

Somewhat disconcerting. What I like about bitcoin is how inflation follows strict rules. If the rules can change at the whim of fallible humans, the foundation of the whole system starts to feel shaky to me.

I have trouble seeing mainstream adoption of a hard fork that messed with actual token issuance. This'll fly since mining power is already fairly consolidated. But devaluing existing tokens by increasing inflation would be a real hard sell to miners.

If a developer released a new bitcoin client that allows for 42 million total bitcoins instead of the current 21 million, no one would upgrade to that new client. The consensus for that change would be "no."

This means that fewer blocks would be uploaded to the blockchain overall, easing network congestion.

This is not correct. The total amount of transactions (per period of time) won't be changed, on average, due to how many transactions can fit in a block at once.
There will still be one block mined every 10 minutes on average. The larger block size limit will allow more transactions to fit into one block keeping transaction confirmation times low.

What do you think about the current trend in medium-large to large business forgoing the traditional systems team to a more devops focused environment?

I think that each side has it's advantages and disadvantages. But I think that having a traditional systems team, although costing more in terms of human resources (and as such finance), a company ends up with more specialized and focsed sysadmins who are capable of determining and resolving issues more rapidly. Although a devops environment allows for more task automation and a common language, if you will, for each member of the team (their development background). If you set your company up at the start with devops, I think it'll be more pragmatic and easier to onboard new blood (to replace old blood) in the long run, but I think a traditional environment would have a hell of a time switching over.

Now that I've given the wishy-washy here's both sides bit: my opinion is that a larger organization benefits from having the specialization of a traditional team. However, I think devops works very well for smaller to medium sized businesses with no intention of wide growth.
